claim: A safety-tuned language model's refusals of harmless requests that merely resemble harmful ones can be cut at decoding time, without training and without weakening refusals of genuinely harmful requests, by contrasting the model's next-token distribution with and without a system prompt that tells it to refuse everything, and then subtracting that refusal signal when the two runs disagree and adding it when they agree. Supported only if, for three model families, it gives the lowest average refusal rate on three over-refusal benchmarks of the decoding, steering, prompting and training-based mitigations compared, while its average refusal rate on three harmful-request sets stays within 0.5 points of the unmodified model; if judged general helpfulness is no lower than the unmodified model's; and if it adds at most 5% to per-token generation time.

experiments: Fix models, data and judging. Setup: Llama3-8B-Instruct, Gemma2-9B-It and Qwen3-8B (thinking disabled), greedy decoding, up to 512 tokens. Over-refusal sets: XSTest safe prompts, ORBench and OKTest; harmful sets: XSTest unsafe prompts, AdvBench and JailBench; general usability on Just-Eval open-ended queries scored by GPT-4 for helpfulness, clarity, factuality, depth and engagement. Refusal and harmfulness judged by WildGuard. Efficiency as average per-token generation time relative to unmodified decoding. The correction is applied only to the first k tokens, with alpha 4.5, switching threshold lambda 0.9 and a plausibility constraint beta 0.01.

Compare with existing mitigations. Setup: unmodified decoding, a prompting method, safety-aware speculative decoding with a trained expert (SSD), removing a precomputed refusal vector from activations (Surgical), and contrastive decoding that always removes the refusal signal (SelfCD), each with its authors' recommended settings. Result (average refusal %, harmless / harmful): Llama3 32.57 / 99.28 default, 19.94 / 91.51 SelfCD, 21.75 / 96.32 Surgical, 16.62 / 99.10 adaptive; Gemma2 41.21 / 99.71, 36.45 / 94.54, 34.86 / 97.21, 32.98 / 99.87; Qwen3 14.77 / 99.44, 8.67 / 93.38, 10.80 / 98.00, 7.89 / 99.68. On average harmless-request refusal falls 10.35 points and harmful-request refusal rises 0.13 points; SSD increases over-refusal on Llama3 (71.97%).

Check general usefulness and speed. Result: Just-Eval average 4.49 against 4.43 unmodified, 4.35 Surgical, 4.24 prompting, 4.23 SSD and 3.88 SelfCD (whose helpfulness falls to 3.63); per-token time 1.02-1.05x unmodified, against 1.98-2.08x for SelfCD and 1.29-1.42x for prompting.

Ablate the two switching criteria. Setup: switch on agreement ratio only or on the confidence constraint only, on XSTest; sweep lambda over 0.3-1.0 on Llama3. Result: removing the agreement ratio raises XSTest-safe refusal to 7.60% (Llama3), 18.80% (Gemma2) and 3.60% (Qwen3) from 1.60, 10.40 and 2.00%; removing the confidence constraint raises it less (3.20%, 11.60%, 2.00%); harmful refusal stays 99-100%; lambda 0.9 gives the best balance.
